slides.title: Tools You’ll Need 🛠️
slides.content:
# Your Local Lab

To follow along, you’ll install:
- **kubectl** – the command‑line tool to talk to any Kubernetes cluster
- **A local cluster** – we recommend **minikube** or **kind** (Kubernetes in Docker)

Both are free, run on Linux/macOS/Windows, and give you a real cluster in minutes.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## If you have Docker Desktop

Docker Desktop includes a built‑in Kubernetes server you can enable with one click. Perfect for this course!

slides.title: Installing kubectl 📥
slides.content:
## The Kubernetes Swiss Army knife

**macOS (Homebrew):**
```bash
brew install kubectl
```

**Windows (Chocolatey):**
```bash
choco install kubernetes-cli
```

**Linux:**
```bash
curl -LO "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -L -s https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl"
chmod +x kubectl
sudo mv kubectl /usr/local/bin/
```

Verify with `kubectl version --client`.

quizData.question: Which command checks your kubectl installation?
quizData.explanation: `kubectl version --client` shows the client version and confirms it's correctly installed.

slides.title: Choosing a Local Cluster 🖥️
slides.content:
## minikube vs kind

| Feature        | minikube                         | kind                                |
|----------------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Focus**      | Full local cluster               | Lightweight, for CI/testing         |
| **Driver**     | VirtualBox, Hyper-V, Docker      | Docker only                         |
| **Startup**    | Slower                           | Fast (containers)                   |
| **Multi‑node** | Possible but extra config        | Easy multi‑node clusters            |

For this course, either is fine. Start one now!
